mainEntity.name: Will the surgery hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant surgery is done under sedation. You feel nothing during it, and you stay relaxed throughout. Afterwards, patients generally report minor discomfort managed with over-the-counter medication.

mainEntity.name: What is recovery like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rest for a few days. Most people are back to normal activity within a week. A soft-food diet is needed for the next several months while the implants integrate with the jawbone.

mainEntity.name: Am I a candidate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many patients already are. Others qualify after preparatory treatment such as bone grafting or extractions. It is not something to guess at. Candidacy is determined properly from a comprehensive consultation and a 3D scan.

mainEntity.name: How long do implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are designed to last decades, and can last the rest of your life. Surgical precision, materials and your own habits are what decide it. Implants have held a published success rate above 95% since they were introduced.

mainEntity.name: Do I still need check-ups?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Implant restorations resist decay, but the gum around an implant can still develop peri-implantitis from plaque and tartar. Brush twice daily, floss once, and keep the six-month hygiene appointments.

mainEntity.name: What does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how many teeth are missing, how long they have been missing, the materials used and whether anything has to be rebuilt first. We file insurance claims on your behalf and can help you apply for financing.

mainEntity.name: Will I leave surgery without teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. In most cases you leave the same visit wearing a fixed PMMA provisional prosthesis, which stays in place while the implants integrate.

mainEntity.name: Can All-on-4 do both jaws?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes: upper, lower, or both. Cases are described here as single arch or double arch for exactly that reason.

mainEntity.name: What if I have bone loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: All-on-4 is often the answer because of bone loss: the rear implants are angled to reach denser bone. Some cases still need grafting first, which the cone-beam scan determines at the consultation.

mainEntity.name: What sedation is available?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nitrous oxide and oral sedation, both given here by the practice’s own team. After oral sedation you need someone to drive you both ways. The practice does not offer IV sedation.

mainEntity.name: How long until it is finished?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three to four months from surgery to the final zirconia prosthesis, then a further two to four months for complete healing around it.

mainEntity.name: Will I be unconscious?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nitrous oxide and oral sedation both leave you awake and responsive. Oral sedation is the deeper of the two: you feel drowsy and relaxed, and some patients remember little of the appointment afterwards. Nitrous is lighter still: you stay awake and simply stop minding. The practice does not offer IV sedation or general anaesthesia.

mainEntity.name: Can I drive myself home?

acceptedAnswer.text: After nitrous oxide, in most cases yes, because recovery is quick. After oral sedation, no: transport to and from the appointment has to be arranged in advance.

mainEntity.name: Is sedation only for surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is available for any procedure. If anxiety or a gag reflex is what has kept you away from routine care, say so when you book.

mainEntity.name: Who administers it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Nahlah’s own clinical team, here in the office. Which of the two suits you depends on the extent of treatment and your personal health, and is settled at the consultation.

mainEntity.name: Do veneers ruin your teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preparation removes less than a millimetre from the front surface of the enamel, enough for the veneer to sit flush instead of bulking the tooth out. It is a permanent modification, which is exactly why the design is agreed and previewed before anything is prepared.

mainEntity.name: Will they stain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain does not stain the way natural enamel does. That is not a reason to change your routine: brush twice a day and floss once, as before.

mainEntity.name: Can veneers fix my bite?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Veneers are a cosmetic treatment for the smile zone. A bad bite is a functional problem and needs to be addressed as one, which is often the reason a prosthodontist is the right person to be assessing it.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take?

acceptedAnswer.text: As few as two appointments once the design is settled: one to prepare and take impressions, one to verify fit and bond.

mainEntity.name: What should I do with a knocked-out tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you can, put the tooth back in its socket and hold it there until you are seen. If you cannot, place it in a small container of milk to preserve it. Do not scrub it clean. Replaced in the socket within the right window and held with a splint, the tooth may be saveable.

mainEntity.name: Why will a toothache not go away?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pain that persists generally means infection, often inside the tooth. Sometimes a filling is the whole answer, but extreme sensitivity or sharp pain when you bite or chew can point to the tooth root, and those cases usually need root canal therapy before the pain can be relieved.

mainEntity.name: Is a broken tooth an emergency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor chips and cracks can wait for a normal appointment. A tooth that is broken or fractured after trauma cannot, because the damage may run past the outside surface into the tooth. You may need a filling, a crown or a root canal; the most severe cases need an emergency extraction.

mainEntity.name: What is dry socket?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dry socket occurs when the blood clot in an empty tooth socket is dislodged, exposing the underlying bone and nerves. It needs treating immediately to prevent infection, usually by cleaning the socket and packing the space with gauze.

mainEntity.name: What is a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three parts: a titanium or ceramic post, an abutment, and a restoration. The post functions as a tooth root does, providing bone support and a stable foundation for a single crown, a bridge, a denture or a full-arch prosthesis.

mainEntity.name: Why are dental implants called the gold standard?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are the only permanent tooth replacement option and are designed to last decades. Because the post is surgically placed into the jawbone, the health and functional benefits are comparable to a natural tooth.

mainEntity.name: What is the success rate of dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Consistently over 95% since implants were introduced decades ago. That comes from the combination of surgical technology, high-quality materials, clinical experience and long-term maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Who is a candidate for dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many patients already are, and many of the rest qualify after preparatory treatment such as bone grafting or extractions. Candidacy is determined accurately only after a comprehensive consultation and evaluation.

mainEntity.name: What is dental implant surgery like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern placement is efficient and precise. Often the procedure is completed in a few hours using patient-fitted surgical guides planned from the scan beforehand.

mainEntity.name: Will dental implant surgery be painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: The surgery is completed while you are under sedation. You will feel no pain, and you stay relaxed throughout.

mainEntity.name: What is recovery from dental implants like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rest for a few days afterwards. Patients generally report minor discomfort that over-the-counter medication handles, and most return to normal activity after about a week. A soft food diet is required for the next several months while the implants integrate with the jawbone.

mainEntity.name: How long does the dental implant process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anywhere from a few months to over a year. If bone grafting is needed first that is a separate procedure with several months of healing. After placement, integration takes three or more months before the final restoration can be permanently attached.

mainEntity.name: How do I care for dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Like natural teeth, with no special maintenance. Brush twice a day and floss once. Depending on the restoration you may need a water flosser to clear debris from underneath it.

mainEntity.name: Do I still need dental check-ups with implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Implant restorations cannot decay, but they can develop peri-implantitis, an infection of the gums around the implant caused by plaque and tartar buildup. Keep the hygiene routine and the six-month visits.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are designed to last decades and have the potential to last the rest of your life. Surgical technology, clinical experience and your own habits all affect it.

mainEntity.name: How much do dental implants cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how many teeth are missing and for how long, the materials used, and what additional procedures are needed first. The practice will help you apply for dental financing and will file insurance claims on your behalf.
